account:
Today’s unusual business seems to centre on the bakery and an evening gathering, although I do not yet know whether they are connected. My neighbour told me that the baker, freight and innkeeper were coordinating a bread order last evening, but did not know its outcome. Several townsfolk have since repeated reports of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery, naming the baker, builder, freight and innkeeper as present. I have not heard a firsthand explanation or seen any crossing change myself. These repeated reports may be the same story spreading rather than independent confirmation. Perhaps they concern transporting bread or supplies, but that is only a possibility.

At this morning’s scheduled mill inspection I found seventy-four hay bales in the mill stall. That establishes the stall’s stock, not whether the bread order was filled. I went to the bakery afterward but did not find the baker to clarify matters.

There is a confirmed eighteen-o’clock great hall meeting about the innkeeper’s community hospitality matter. The appointment says I should attend alone and need no preparation; the secretary has agreed to remind and escort me. It might concern the bread arrangements, but I have no evidence establishing that connection or a more specific purpose.

Otherwise I have kept my ordinary appointments: morning office hours, the mill visit, lunch at home, and now the thirteen-o’clock council letters session. I have just asked the secretary whether correspondence has arrived and await an answer. Earlier this morning none had been delivered, and the custodian of the financial records remained unidentified. Tea with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage is due at fifteen, followed by office hours at sixteen-thirty.
